title: Conflict detection, parking, and mechanical resolution
summary: A PR whose merge state goes CONFLICTING is picked up on the parked-pr-conflict-watch's 120s sweep across THREE populations — parked (already under a review hold), queued (approved, drain gets first try), and unowned (no review-workflow label at all) — labelled, then routed to a mechanical rebase, a fix-agent bounce, or a human stand-down. A stacked PR (base isn't main) is deferred entirely to reconcile-core.mjs's own stacked-rebase branch instead. Separately, when a PR's base merges, the DRAIN (not this watch) proactively retargets any PR stacked on it before the base branch is deleted, or the stacked PR is closed by GitHub with no automatic recovery.

states.label: PR's merge state reads CONFLICTING (DIRTY/BEHIND)
states.owner: scripts/conveyor/parked-pr-conflict-watch.mjs sweep — classifies every OPEN PR (no label filter) into parked / queued / unowned
states.notes: defaultListParkedPrs (parked-pr-conflict-watch.mjs:1169-1180) runs `gh pr list --state open` with NO label filter — every open PR is classified fresh each ~120s sweep (DEFAULT_PASS_INTERVAL_MS, skills-src/conveyor/daemon-manifest.mjs:29, wired per-repo at :162). Three populations, in priority order: parked (isParkedConflictTarget, :181-190 — an uncleared review:human/pending/changes hold), queued (isQueuedConflictTarget, :202-210 — review:accepted/ready-to-merge, no hold), unowned (isUnownedConflictTarget, :220-226 — neither of the above, base equal to main/unknown). Before commit 93b2d603a (an ancestor of this repo's current main), the unowned population did not exist and a conflicting PR with no review-workflow label sat 'owed-elsewhere' forever (reconcile-core.mjs:1122) with nothing else picking it up — the file's own header (:69-114) names the live incident, web-everything/web-everything#2709. That gap is closed for a main-base PR as of this commit; reconcile-core.mjs itself STILL never dispatches a mechanical fix for a bare `conflicted` phase (reconcile-core.mjs:1122, OWED_ELSEWHERE.conflicted refusal) — it relies entirely on this watch to be 'elsewhere'.

states.label: Approved + queued PR conflicting — drain gets first try

wait.for: the drain to auto-heal a shared-manifest-only conflict, or the grace window to expire

states.notes: QUEUED_CONFLICT_GRACE_MS=30min (:191) only applies when computeConflictDisposition reads the conflict as manifest-only/clean (:1392-1399) — a REAL non-manifest conflict skips the wait entirely and routes immediately (:1400-1403, 'never worth waiting out the drain's turn on'). A stacked-base PR reaching this branch is deferred straight to reconcile-core's stacked-rebase branch instead, with no grace semantics at all (:1408-1418) — see stacked-base-deferred-to-fix. A persistently unreadable age source used to wait past grace forever; #4118(b) falls back to this watch's own alert-comment timestamp before giving up (:1408-1414).

states.label: No review-workflow label — mechanical rebase-drop attempted at once, no grace

retries.what: unowned-rebase-attempt-count.mjs#countUnownedRebaseAttempts — a durable, PR-comment-backed count of this population's own retry-worthy ('skip'/'error', including a caught throw) rebase-drop attempts; a clean 'rebased'/'current' success posts no marker

states.notes: #4230 (epic #4075/#3383) — FIXED. Reuses the SAME proven, no-checkout rebase-drop plumbing the drain uses (:323-337). Runs on the SAME sweep that first detects the PR, before any label or bounce (:89 docblock) — gets NO grace period, unlike the queued population. On `action:'rebased'`/`'current'` it resolves silently: no label, no bounce, GitHub's own mergeable flips on the next read. An `action:'skip'`/`'error'` result already fell through to the ordinary bounce within the SAME sweep (inheriting `bounced-to-fix`'s own CONFLICT_FIX_ROUND_CAP) — the gap was a THROW from the git-level attempt itself aborting the whole per-PR handler before any label ever applied, silently retrying forever with nothing durable recording it. The attempt is now wrapped so a throw becomes `{action:'error'}` instead of escaping (parked-pr-conflict-watch.mjs:1626-1627), and a durable marker (UNOWNED_REBASE_ATTEMPT_MARKER) is posted the moment the outcome is known to be `skip`/`error` (never on a clean success) so the count survives even a throw, before anything downstream of it (the comment/dispatch/label writes) gets a chance to fail too. At the cap, this state routes to `unowned-rebase-cap-exhausted` instead of attempting again.

states.label: Unowned rebase-drop attempt cap (3) exhausted — refused AND surfaced

escalation.how: round-cap-exhausted note (capKind: unowned-mechanical-rebase) → PR comment (#2725 reconcile-notes channel) + a health-watch-style desktop notify

states.notes: #4230 (epic #4075/#3383) — FIXED. Mirrors review.flow.json's own `round-cap-exhausted` state exactly: reuses the SAME `kind:'round-cap-exhausted'` note shape (reconcile-note-comment.mjs), here with `capKind:'unowned-mechanical-rebase'` naming THIS population, and `notifyDesktopChecked` (branch-sync.mjs) for the immediate desktop-visible half, mirroring health-watch's own minimal notify path. Once surfaced, the PR falls through to the ordinary bounce (bounced-to-fix) below, exactly like a `skip`/`error` disposition already did — this state is the surfaced-cap-exhaustion landing point, not a dead end for the PR itself. `retries.onCap` self-loops (nothing retries FROM here; a human clears it, e.g. by resolving the underlying failure and letting the PR re-conflict fresh).

states.label: Labelled + bounced to review:changes — mechanical conflict-fix owed
states.owner: scripts/conveyor/parked-pr-conflict-watch.mjs#defaultPostConflictFinding, then scripts/conveyor/reconcile-core.mjs's isConflictBounce dispatch (the fix flow)
states.notes: postFinding posts a comment + CONFLICT_LABEL and strips review:accepted/ready-to-merge (fresh path :1608-1619,1655-1658; after-grace path :1463-1467). Once phase reads 'bounced' + CONFLICT_LABEL, reconcile-core.mjs's isConflictBounce branch (reconcile-core.mjs:1211-1234) dispatches a real fix agent under kind:'fix' — this is the SAME 'pr-flagged-for-fix' state the fix.flow.json flow owns from here, including its own CONFLICT_FIX_ROUND_CAP=3 cap-exhaustion handling (reconcile-core.mjs:1215-1219). This watch keeps re-sweeping the PR every tick regardless (idempotent: already-labelled means no new finding is posted) until mergeable flips back to MERGEABLE.

states.label: Statute-tier judgment call — handed to a human

wait.for: a human to clear the stand-down (or take the PR over via /finish)

escalation.how: durable PR comment (STAND_DOWN_MARKER), idempotent — never re-posted while it stands

states.notes: Shells stand-down.mjs --reason=conflict (parked-pr-conflict-watch.mjs:1207-1214); reconcile-core.mjs's countUnresolvedStandDowns gate (reconcile-core.mjs:472-485,822-847) refuses any further dispatch for this PR while it stands. NOT permanently frozen, though: a PARKED review:human PR that is ALREADY labelled+stood-down is RE-CHECKED every sweep (the #3557 'recheckCandidate' fork, parked-pr-conflict-watch.mjs:1300-1365) — if it now classifies as append-only-statute or review-human-fixable, the earlier stand-down is explicitly SUPERSEDED and routed to a fix agent instead (SUPERSEDE_STAND_DOWN_MARKER, stand-down.mjs:138; parked-pr-conflict-watch.mjs:1350-1362).

states.label: GitHub reports MERGEABLE again
states.notes: Read fresh every sweep off the SAME classification, so this fires regardless of which upstream state the PR was in (bounced-to-fix, stacked-base-deferred-to-fix, stood-down, or unowned-mechanical-rebase-attempt via GitHub's own recompute). Branches at :1621-1662 on whether a re-arm is even owed (needsRearm = the PR still carries review:changes — false for a stacked/never-bounced PR, which just gets its label removed directly with review:accepted untouched, :1646-1651).

states.label: Resolved, but a fix agent is still live on this PR — rearm withheld

wait.for: the live fix session (role==='fix', name-based liveness) to finish

escalation.how: liveness-wait-exhausted note → PR comment (#2725 reconcile-notes channel) + a health-watch-style desktop notify, once per episode

states.notes: #4230 (epic #4075/#3383) — FIXED. CONFLICT_LABEL is deliberately left ON so newlyResolved re-fires next sweep (:1740-1743) — a DIFFERENT, name-based liveness check from reconcile-core.mjs#assessLiveness (own import comment explains why). A durable, episode-scoped marker (REARM_DEFERRED_MARKER) records the FIRST sweep this deferral was observed; past 90 minutes since then (mirrors reconcile-core.mjs's own LIVE_SESSION_OVERRUN_MS bound and reasoning — a name-based liveness read staying true this long is far more likely stale than a real 90-minute fix round), this file surfaces it via the SAME reconcile-notes channel + desktop notify every other cap-exhaustion state in this repo uses, rather than forcing a rearm (which would race the exact liveness gap #4118 (c) introduced this wait to avoid). `wait.onTimeout` self-loops: the PR keeps deferring (dedup'd — one note per episode) until a human clears the stale liveness read or the fixer genuinely finishes.

states.label: Re-armed for re-review — conflict watch's job on this PR is done
states.notes: postRearm (parked-pr-conflict-watch.mjs:1654-1655) shells rearm-review.mjs, which swaps review:changes->review:pending and posts REARM_COMMENT_MARKER (scripts/conveyor/rearm-review.mjs:40,73-78) — 'the SAME sanctioned hand-back an ordinary repaired bounce uses.' For a stacked/never-bounced PR (needsRearm false) this state is reached with only the label removed, no rearm comment posted — the PR's prior review:accepted/whatever rides through untouched.

states.label: A PR's base is about to be deleted by another PR merging
states.owner: scripts/lib/pr-merge-gate.mjs#retargetStackedPrs, called from the DRAIN (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs) — NOT owned by this flow's own watch/reconcile daemons
states.notes: mergePr always merges --delete-branch (scripts/lib/pr-merge-gate.mjs:187-193); GitHub's behaviour on a deleted base is to CLOSE any PR still based on it, never retarget it (confirmed live recovering web-everything/web-everything#2578). retargetStackedPrs (pr-merge-gate.mjs:218-239) runs a `gh pr edit --base <default>` per open stacked PR BEFORE the merge that deletes the base (called scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:4897-4905), proactively — this is NOT a passive wait on GitHub's own auto-retarget (GitHub does not reliably do that here). Best-effort by design (pr-merge-gate.mjs:210-215): a `gh` miss here must never block the base PR's own merge.

states.label: Retarget failed — GitHub closes the stacked PR

escalation.how: durable PR comment posted BEFORE the close (buildStackedBaseCloseReason), naming the recovery: re-target onto the default branch on a fresh PR, or run the #3383 recovery path

states.notes: On a failed retarget (scripts/lib/pr-merge-gate.mjs:236-239 `failed[]`), scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:4906 posts a durable comment naming the closure and recovery BEFORE the base-deleting merge runs (:2300-2320) — GitHub permits neither a retarget nor a reopen once the PR has actually closed (verified live recovering web-everything/web-everything#2578), so 'after' would be too late. Recovery from here is explicitly a HUMAN action (re-target a fresh PR, or an operator running the #3383 recovery path) — nothing in this file set retries or auto-recovers a closed PR.

states.label: Stacked-base conflict — deferred entirely to the fix flow's stacked-rebase branch
states.owner: scripts/conveyor/parked-pr-conflict-watch.mjs (labels only), then scripts/conveyor/reconcile-core.mjs's STACKED-BASE CONFLICT branch (the fix flow)
states.notes: A PR whose baseRefName isn't main/unknown is never landed by the drain regardless of label (#poc-branch-declared-delivery-mode clause 5), so the ordinary grace/bounce machinery does not apply — this watch only applies CONFLICT_LABEL immediately (both from queued-grace at :1408-1418 and from fresh detection at :1494-1498) and reports the deferral; it posts NO comment and touches NO other label for this population. reconcile-core.mjs's STACKED-BASE CONFLICT branch (reconcile-core.mjs:1062-1119) then dispatches the actual mechanical rebase under kind:'fix', mode:'stacked-rebase', reading baseRefName LIVE off the PR at repair time so a since-retargeted PR (see stacked-pr-orphan-risk) is read correctly even if this row was planned a tick earlier against the old base (reconcile-core.mjs:1082-1094). Shares the SAME CONFLICT_FIX_ROUND_CAP=3 as the ordinary bounce (reconcile-core.mjs:1097-1107) — documented in fix.flow.json's own round-cap-hit state, not duplicated here.

transitions.on: queued (approved, no uncleared hold) — give the drain first try
unowned (no review-workflow label at all)
parked (already under an uncleared review hold), real (non-mechanical) content conflict — labelled and bounced at once
fresh detection already classifies as statute-tier and not mechanically resolvable
PR's own base isn't main — deferred whole-cloth to the fix flow's stacked-rebase branch
30-minute grace expires (manifest-only case), or a real conflict skips the wait outright
post-grace re-classification is statute-tier and not mechanically resolvable
PR's own base isn't main, discovered once grace-checked
rebase-drop succeeds (action:'rebased'/'current') — GitHub recomputes mergeable clean, no label ever applied
rebase-drop reports 'skip' (a real conflict), 'error' (a plumbing failure, including a caught throw) — falls through to the ordinary bounce
the durable per-PR attempt count already >= 3 (UNOWNED_REBASE_ATTEMPT_CAP)
surfaced once, then falls through to the ordinary bounce the SAME sweep
a fix agent is dispatched to resolve the mechanical conflict
mergeable flips back to MERGEABLE on a later sweep
reconcile-core.mjs dispatches the mechanical stacked-rebase
mergeable flips back to MERGEABLE on a later sweep
re-check finds it now append-only-statute or review-human-fixable — the earlier stand-down is explicitly superseded
a human resolves the conflict by hand while it stood down
review:changes still carried AND a fix agent's role still reads live on this PR
no live fix agent (or nothing needed rearming in the first place) — rearm/label-removal proceeds now
the live fix session finishes and liveness reads clear on a later sweep
retarget succeeds — the PR's baseRefName is now main; a fresh conflict against main (if any) is picked up by the ordinary populations
retarget fails and the base branch is deleted by the merge

steps.does: lists every OPEN PR with no label filter, then classifies each as parked / queued / unowned / none
ensures + applies CONFLICT_LABEL and posts the bounce finding (review:changes)
